item.title: Reverse-a-function drill: bsr highest set bit
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64 (arg in `ecx`).
Reverse this short function to equivalent C:
```asm mystery: or ecx, 1 bsr eax, ecx ret ```
What does it return for 0, 1, 2 and 1000? Why the `or`?
ANSWER ## Answer
```c unsigned mystery(unsigned x) { x |= 1; return 31 - __builtin_clz(x); // index of highest set bit = floor(log2(x)) } ```
Results: 0 → 0, 1 → 0, 2 → 1, 1000 → 9.
## Explanation
- `bsr` (0F BD) scans from bit 31 down and returns the index of the highest set bit, i.e. floor(log2(x)). - With a zero source, `bsr` sets ZF and leaves the destination undefined, so `or ecx, 1` guarantees a nonzero input. - Setting bit 0 never changes the highest set bit of a nonzero x, so only x = 0 is affected (it returns 0).
